name: Africa
blurb: Music, movies, ancient empires, modern history, food, wildlife and more from all 54 nations of the continent.

clues.q: This Nigerian star, born Damini Ogulu, won the Grammy for Best Global Music Album in 2021 for “Twice as Tall.”
Born in Ghana in the early 20th century, this guitar- and horn-driven dance music later inspired the fusion genre “hiplife.”
Emerging from South Africa's townships in the 2010s, this house-music style is known for its deep “log drum” basslines.
Nicknamed “Mama Africa,” this South African singer had an international hit in 1967 with “Pata Pata.”
This Senegalese mbalax superstar recorded the 1994 hit “7 Seconds” with Neneh Cherry.
Nigeria's hugely prolific film industry is known by this nickname.
This 1994 Disney animated film, set in the Pride Lands, opens with the song “Circle of Life.”
This 2018 Marvel film starring Chadwick Boseman is set in the fictional African nation of Wakanda.
Lupita Nyong'o, who grew up in Kenya, won the Best Supporting Actress Oscar for this 2013 film directed by Steve McQueen.
This 2005 Johannesburg-set film directed by Gavin Hood won the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
Howard Carter discovered this boy king's nearly intact tomb in the Valley of the Kings in 1922.
Found in 1799, this stone slab carries the same decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic and ancient Greek scripts.
In 218 BCE this Carthaginian general famously marched an army with war elephants across the Alps to attack Rome.
The ruins of the great Phoenician city of Carthage lie in what is now this North African country.
The Great Pyramid of Giza was built as the tomb of this Fourth Dynasty pharaoh, known to the Greeks as Cheops.
In 1994, Nelson Mandela was elected president of this country.
In 1957, the British colony of the Gold Coast became independent under this new name.
Founded in Addis Ababa in 1963, this continental body was replaced by the African Union in 2002.
clues.a: What is the Organisation of African Unity (OAU)?

clues.q: In 1956, Egypt's Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalized this waterway linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
In 2011, this country gained independence from Sudan after a referendum.
Generally considered Africa's longest river, it flows north through Egypt into the Mediterranean.
Africa's highest mountain, this snow-capped dormant volcano rises in northern Tanzania.
Which of these is the largest country in Africa by area?
This island nation in the Indian Ocean, the world's fourth-largest island, is famous for its Avenue of the Baobabs.
Shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, this is Africa's largest lake by area.
This spongy, slightly sour flatbread made from teff flour is the base of Ethiopian and Eritrean meals.
Cooks in Nigeria, Ghana and Senegal playfully argue over who makes the best version of this tomato-based rice dish.
This North African staple of tiny steamed semolina granules is often served under a meat or vegetable stew.
This slow-cooked Moroccan stew shares its name with the cone-lidded clay pot it is cooked in.
This South African snack of cured, air-dried strips of meat is often compared to jerky.
This Nigerian bandleader and activist pioneered Afrobeat and performed at his Lagos club, the Shrine.
This singer from Benin won the 2008 Grammy for Best Contemporary World Music Album for “Djin Djin.”
This Nigerian star featured on Drake's “One Dance,” which topped the Billboard Hot 100 in 2016.
Associated with the Algerian port city of Oran, this popular genre made stars of Khaled and Cheb Mami.
This Malian guitarist won a Grammy with Ry Cooder for the 1994 album “Talking Timbuktu.”
In this 1988 comedy, Eddie Murphy plays Prince Akeem of Zamunda, who travels to Queens to find a bride.
This 2009 Neill Blomkamp sci-fi film is set in Johannesburg, where stranded extraterrestrials are confined to a camp.
This 1942 Humphrey Bogart classic takes its title from the Moroccan city where it is set.
Chiwetel Ejiofor directed and starred in this 2019 film about a Malawian teenager who builds a windmill to pump water for his village's fields.
clues.a: What is The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind?

clues.q: Filmmaker Ousmane Sembène, often called the “father of African cinema,” came from this West African country.
The last active ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, this queen allied with Julius Caesar and later Mark Antony.
This Macedonian conqueror founded Egypt's great port city, later home to a famous library, in 331 BCE.
The ancient Nubian kingdom of Kush, whose kings once ruled Egypt as its 25th Dynasty, lay in what is now this country.
This 14th-century ruler of the Mali Empire became legendary for the wealth he displayed on his pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324.
This ancient kingdom in today's Ethiopia and Eritrea is famous for its towering carved stone stelae.
This leader spent 27 years in prison before becoming South Africa's first Black president.
He led Kenya to independence in 1963 and became the country's first president.
In 2004, this founder of Kenya's Green Belt Movement became the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.
Elected in 2005, Ellen Johnson Sirleaf became Africa's first elected female head of state in this country.
Tanzania's founding president was affectionately known by the Swahili title “Mwalimu,” meaning “teacher.”
The world's tallest land animal, it browses on acacia leaves across the African savanna.
The fastest land animal, this spotted cat hunts by sprinting across open grasslands.
Each year, well over a million of these bearded antelopes migrate between Tanzania's Serengeti and Kenya's Maasai Mara.
Mountain gorillas live in the volcanic Virunga Mountains, shared by DR Congo, Uganda and this country.
Found only in the rainforests of DR Congo, this shy animal with zebra-striped legs is actually a relative of the giraffe.
Widely spoken in Kenya and Tanzania, this Bantu language gave English the word “safari.”
This language is the most widely spoken in Egypt and across North Africa.
Afrikaans, spoken in South Africa and Namibia, developed mainly from which European language?
Ethiopia's main working language, it is written in a script descended from ancient Ge'ez.
Nelson Mandela's mother tongue, this Southern African language is famous for its click consonants.

questions.q: Country home to the city of Timbuktu?
Island nation where the dodo lived?
Country completely surrounded by South Africa?
Official language of Angola and Mozambique?
World's largest bird, native to Africa?

clues.q: This South African a cappella group won worldwide fame singing on Paul Simon's 1986 album “Graceland.”
clues.hint: Their name includes a South African town.

clues.q: This Ivorian singer is one of Africa's best-known reggae artists, with songs like “Jerusalem.”
clues.hint: His stage name begins with a Greek letter.

clues.q: This Nigerian singer's 2022 hit “Calm Down” became a global smash after a remix with Selena Gomez.
clues.hint: A short, four-letter stage name.

clues.q: Nicknamed the “Barefoot Diva,” this Cape Verdean singer brought morna music to audiences worldwide.
clues.hint: She grew up in Mindelo on the island of São Vicente.

clues.q: Malian virtuoso Toumani Diabaté was a master of this 21-string West African harp-lute with a calabash body.
clues.hint: A four-letter instrument of the griots.

clues.q: Based on Karen Blixen's memoir of her Kenyan coffee farm, this 1985 Meryl Streep–Robert Redford film won Best Picture.
clues.hint: The title names the whole continent.

clues.q: Charlize Theron, born in Benoni, South Africa, won the Best Actress Oscar for this 2003 film.
clues.hint: She played real-life Aileen Wuornos.

clues.q: Born Michel Shalhoub in Alexandria, this Egyptian actor starred in “Lawrence of Arabia” and “Doctor Zhivago.”
clues.hint: His first name is also a famous Arabic name.

clues.q: This 2009 Clint Eastwood film shows Nelson Mandela and the Springboks during the 1995 Rugby World Cup.
clues.hint: Its title is Latin for “unconquered.”

clues.q: Abderrahmane Sissako's 2014 Mauritanian film, an Oscar nominee, is named after this historic city in Mali.
clues.hint: A city once famed for its manuscripts.

clues.q: Jean-François Champollion made the breakthrough in deciphering this ancient Egyptian writing system in 1822.
clues.hint: Picture-like symbols carved on temple walls.

clues.q: This female pharaoh of the 18th Dynasty built a famous terraced mortuary temple at Deir el-Bahari.
clues.hint: She was often depicted wearing a false beard.

clues.q: Built from the 11th to the 15th centuries, this stone city's ruins gave their name to a modern nation.
clues.hint: Its name means roughly “houses of stone.”

clues.q: This Kushite city on the Nile in modern Sudan, a later royal capital, is surrounded by about 200 steep-sided pyramids.
clues.hint: Its name starts with M.

clues.q: Born in Leptis Magna in what is now Libya, this man became Roman emperor in 193 CE.
clues.hint: He founded the Severan dynasty.

clues.q: Africa's most populous country, it gained independence from Britain on October 1, 1960.
clues.hint: Its largest city is Lagos.

clues.q: In 1964, Tanganyika united with this Indian Ocean island to form Tanzania.
clues.hint: Famous for spices and Stone Town.

clues.q: This Anglican cleric, later archbishop of Cape Town, won the 1984 Nobel Peace Prize for his nonviolent opposition to apartheid.
clues.hint: Often called “the Arch.”

clues.q: Which country became independent from Ethiopia in 1993 after a referendum?
clues.hint: Its capital is Asmara.

clues.q: This Ghanaian diplomat served as UN Secretary-General from 1997 to 2006 and shared the 2001 Nobel Peace Prize.
clues.hint: His first name is an Akan day name.

clues.q: This Liberian striker, the 1995 FIFA World Player of the Year, was elected his country's president in 2017.
clues.hint: He starred for AC Milan.

clues.q: Ethiopia's Abebe Bikila won the 1960 Olympic marathon in Rome while running this way.
clues.hint: Think about his feet.

clues.q: Nicknamed the “Indomitable Lions,” this nation reached the men's World Cup quarterfinals in 1990.
clues.hint: Roger Milla danced at the corner flag.

clues.q: In 2022 in Qatar, this nation became the first African team to reach a men's World Cup semifinal.
clues.hint: Nicknamed the Atlas Lions.

clues.q: In 2019 in Vienna, this Kenyan became the first person to run the marathon distance in under two hours.
clues.hint: Two-time Olympic marathon champion.

clues.q: Carved from limestone, this giant statue with a lion's body and a human head guards the Giza plateau.
clues.hint: Famous for a riddle in Greek myth.

clues.q: Known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya, “the smoke that thunders,” this waterfall lies on the Zambia–Zimbabwe border.
clues.hint: Named after a British queen.

clues.q: This flat-topped mountain, often draped in a “tablecloth” of cloud, looms over Cape Town.
clues.hint: Named for a piece of furniture.

clues.q: This Ethiopian town is famous for its medieval churches hewn from solid rock below ground level.
clues.hint: Named after a 12th–13th-century king.

clues.q: Rebuilt in 1907, the towering mud-brick Great Mosque of this Malian city is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
clues.hint: An inland Niger Delta trading city.

clues.q: Born David Adeleke, this Afrobeats star had a long-charting hit in 2017 with “Fall.”
clues.hint: His stage name echoes his first name.

clues.q: Born Temilade Openiyi, this Nigerian singer won a Grammy for her part on Future's “Wait for U.”
clues.hint: A short nickname from her first name.

clues.q: This South African trumpeter topped the U.S. charts in 1968 with the instrumental “Grazing in the Grass.”
clues.hint: Once married to Miriam Makeba.

clues.q: This blind married duo from Mali released the acclaimed 2004 album “Dimanche à Bamako.”
clues.hint: Two first names joined by “and.”

clues.q: Called “the Star of the East,” this Egyptian singer drew the whole Arab world to her monthly radio concerts.
clues.hint: Famed for the hour-long love song “Enta Omri.”

clues.q: Humphrey Bogart won his only Oscar for this 1951 film about a riverboat journey in German East Africa.
clues.hint: The boat gives the film its name.

clues.q: Two-time Oscar nominee Djimon Hounsou, of “In America” and “Blood Diamond,” was born in this West African country.
clues.hint: Its largest city is Cotonou.

clues.q: This director of the 1958 classic “Cairo Station” received Cannes' 50th Anniversary Prize for his body of work in 1997.
clues.hint: Egypt's most celebrated film director.

clues.q: Set in Soweto, this 1992 musical drama starring Whoopi Goldberg was adapted from a stage show.
clues.hint: Named after its student heroine.

clues.q: Mati Diop's 2019 film set in Dakar won the Grand Prix at Cannes.
clues.hint: A ghostly love story about young workers who leave by sea.

clues.q: Often called “the Great,” this 19th Dynasty pharaoh built the colossal rock temples at Abu Simbel.
clues.hint: He reigned for about 66 years.

clues.q: Rome destroyed Carthage in 146 BCE at the end of this series of three wars.
clues.hint: From the Latin word for Phoenician.

clues.q: This pharaoh promoted worship of the sun disk Aten and built a new capital at Amarna.
clues.hint: Husband of Nefertiti.

clues.q: Centered on Gao, this West African empire expanded rapidly in the 15th century under Sonni Ali.
clues.hint: It succeeded Mali as the region's great power.

clues.q: Ruling around the 330s CE, this king of Aksum adopted Christianity and issued coins bearing the cross.
clues.hint: A five-letter name starting with E.

clues.q: Ghana's first prime minister and president, he was a leading voice of Pan-Africanism.
clues.hint: His first name is the Akan name for Saturday.

clues.q: Formerly called South West Africa, this country became independent in 1990.
clues.hint: Its capital is Windhoek.

clues.q: Formerly Upper Volta, this West African country adopted its current name, meaning “land of upright people,” in 1984.
clues.hint: Its capital is Ouagadougou.

clues.q: In 1977, this small nation on the Horn of Africa gained independence from France.
clues.hint: Its capital shares the country's name.

clues.q: In 1955, leaders of 29 Asian and African nations, including Egypt, Ethiopia and Liberia, met at this gathering in Indonesia.
clues.a: What is the Bandung Conference (Asian–African Conference)?
clues.hint: Held in a city on the island of Java.

clues.q: Chinua Achebe's 1958 novel follows Okonkwo, a proud Igbo wrestler and leader.
clues.hint: Its title comes from a Yeats poem.

clues.q: This Nigerian author wrote “Half of a Yellow Sun,” “Americanah” and the essay “We Should All Be Feminists.”
clues.hint: Her TED talks are famous too.

clues.q: This Nigerian playwright and poet won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986.
clues.hint: Author of “Death and the King's Horseman.”

clues.q: This Egyptian novelist, author of the Cairo Trilogy, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1988.
clues.hint: The Arab world's first Nobel literature laureate.

clues.q: The Kenyan author of “Petals of Blood” later chose to write mainly in his native Gikuyu.
clues.hint: Also wrote “Decolonising the Mind.”

clues.q: The world's largest hot desert, it stretches across much of North Africa.
clues.hint: Its name comes from Arabic for “desert.”

clues.q: This coastal desert on Africa's southwestern Atlantic shore is famous for the towering red dunes of Sossusvlei.
clues.hint: It shares its root with the country's name.

clues.q: The Okavango Delta, a vast inland delta that floods each year, is in which country?
clues.hint: Its capital is Gaborone.

clues.q: Running from the Afar region down through East Africa, this huge fault system cradles Lakes Tanganyika and Malawi.
clues.a: What is the Great Rift Valley (East African Rift)?
clues.hint: Tectonic plates are slowly pulling apart here.

clues.q: This vast volcanic caldera in northern Tanzania shelters lions, rhinos and elephants on its floor.
clues.hint: Neighbors the Serengeti.

questions.q: Which of these East African countries is landlocked?
Which Moroccan spice blend's name means roughly “head of the shop”?
Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World stood at Alexandria?
The Moroccan mountain town of Chefchaouen is famous for walls painted in shades of what color?
The Swahili phrase “hakuna matata,” popularized by a Disney film, means “no ___.” Fill in the blank.
What is the currency of Ghana?
Which river flows through Bamako and Niamey?
Which country's national football team is nicknamed “Les Éléphants”?
Africa's second-highest mountain shares its name with which country?
In which Moroccan city is the bustling Jemaa el-Fnaa square?

rounds.name: Final Round
rounds.q: It is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still largely standing, and it was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for more than 3,800 years.
rounds.a: What is the Great Pyramid of Giza?
rounds.hint: Built for a Fourth Dynasty pharaoh near Cairo.

rounds.name: Final Round
rounds.q: This mighty Central African river crosses the equator twice and is the world's deepest recorded river, with depths of over 200 meters.
rounds.hint: It shares its name with two countries.
